text:
Marta (Marketing Lead): Quick sync — we need a tight benchmark narrative for next Tue's webinar. Goal: 90s demo + 2 hero charts for email/landing that show latency vs $/1k tokens tradeoff. keep messaging focused on production economics, not raw model names.
Jason (Growth): Agree — lean funnel copy. Can we show a clear 'your latency' bucket with expected $ savings for typical SaaS calls? :thinking_face:
Ben (Product Marketing): Yes. Proposal: 2 charts — (1) latency vs cost lines for common model families, normalized to 100ms baseline; (2) a savings heatmap: prompt length vs % cost reduction when using caching/batching.
Anya (Design): I can mock compact versions for hero and social. Need precise axes and a tiny caption. prefer simplified palette (blue/red/amber) for clarity.
Leo (Analytics): I can generate data from last quarter's synthetic workload. Quick sketch of the data model: 1) base tokens per call distributions (50/200/800) 2) seq length tails 99th pct 3) batching factor effects.
Marta: Great. Can you produce two sample CSVs by EOD? We'll need one for the hero line chart and one for the heatmap.
Leo: Will do. Example output I'll drop:
```
# hero_lines.csv
latency_ms,redwood_quant,open_standard
50,0.04,0.09
100,0.06,0.12
200,0.09,0.2
500,0.18,0.4
```
and
```
# heatmap.csv
prompt_len_bucket,cache_enabled_pct,cost_reduction_pct
0-50,10,5
51-200,40,22
201-1000,70,45
```
Ben: Nice. For narrative copy — headline option A: "Same output quality, fewer dollars and predictable latency." Option B: "Ship fast without paying more." Thoughts?
Jason (Growth): A feels more enterprise-focused. A/B test both on email subject lines.
Anya: For the hero caption keep under 12 words. Suggest: "Latency vs cost: choose the sweet spot for production inference."
Marta: Love it. Ops ask: can we call out typical savings for SMB vs Enterprise so SDR routing works? e.g., SMB likely sees X% savings with batching; enterprise sees Y% with dedicated.
Leo: I can estimate buckets — SMB avg call 120 tokens, batching x4 → ~18-25% cost reduction; Enterprise avg 450 tokens, caching → ~40-55% on repeat prompts. I'll include ranges and confidence intervals.
Jason: Routing idea: use the lead form (hidden field) with estimated savings bucket (low/med/high) and map to SDR tier. Creative to include a micro calc on landing: "Estimate your % savings" link.
Anya: I'll add a small interactive microcalc wireframe to the Figma mock. link: https://figma.com/file/Example123 (placeholder)
Marta: Timeline: Leo CSV + quick charts by EOD, Anya mock by EOD+next morning, Ben copy draft tomorrow morning. We need final assets by Mon so growth can prep ASO/email.
OpsBot: Reminder set: @Marta scheduled check-in tomorrow 11:00am PT.
Ben: One more angle: competitor framing — avoid naming, instead say "common managed endpoints" vs "Redwood inference with batching & cache". Keep claims verifiable.
Marta: Agreed. We'll include a short methodology note in the slide deck: sampling, normalization, and assumptions. Ben, can you draft that section?
Ben: On it. I'll put a 3-bullet methodology note and a link to the raw CSV in the deck.
Jason: For webinar promo: hero chart as the second slide, one-liner in subject tested A/B, CTA to microcalc. I'll draft email 1 after assets.
Marta: Perfect. If no blockers, everyone proceed. Ping here when you upload CSVs/mock. Thanks :raised_hands:
Leo: Uploaded hero_lines.csv and heatmap.csv to the shared drive: https://drive.company/s/benchmark-assets (will update with exact path)
Anya: Figma frame uploaded (hero + microcalc) — commenting on colors for accessibility.
Ben: Draft methodology and copy added to the deck.
Jason: Draft email ready for review, linking to the microcalc.
Marta: Excellent — final sync Monday 9am PT to approve.
